locator: Table ES.1, p. ES-2; Study Methods, pp. 7–13.
context: Texas Summer Bridge randomized evaluation; implementation, enrollment and one-year academic outcomes remain distinct.
name: Texas Summer Bridge randomly assigned 1,318 students across eight colleges.
description: The 2009 experiment assigned 793 students to program eligibility and 525 to colleges’ regular services. It evaluates a varied multi-site model, not one uniform college program.

context: Texas Summer Bridge randomized evaluation; implementation, enrollment and one-year academic outcomes remain distinct.
name: Texas Summer Bridge required $1,319 per admitted student across eight sites (2009 dollars).
description: This source-reported resource requirement includes staffing, other costs, student resources, and a 30% overhead assumption. Some costs may be start-up costs; it is not a net cost or cost-effectiveness result.

values.value: 2009 USD average resource cost per admitted student across eight sites.

context: Texas Summer Bridge randomized evaluation; implementation, enrollment and one-year academic outcomes remain distinct.
name: Texas Summer Bridge increased attempts at a first college-level math course by 8.7 percentage points (15.1% versus 6.5%).
description: This is an intent-to-treat fall-2009 course-progression result, not a degree or persistence effect.

values.value: Percentage-point difference in attempting a first college-level math course in fall 2009, program minus control.

context: Texas Summer Bridge randomized evaluation; implementation, enrollment and one-year academic outcomes remain distinct.
name: Texas Summer Bridge increased passing a first college-level math course by 4.4 percentage points (8.8% versus 4.4%).
description: This is an intent-to-treat fall-2009 course outcome in a preliminary one-year report.

values.value: Percentage-point difference in passing a first college-level math course in fall 2009, program minus control.

context: Texas Summer Bridge randomized evaluation; implementation, enrollment and one-year academic outcomes remain distinct.
name: Texas Summer Bridge increased passing a first college-level writing course by 5.1 percentage points (32.0% versus 26.9%).
description: This is an intent-to-treat fall-2009 course outcome, not later persistence or completion.

values.value: Percentage-point difference in passing a first college-level writing course in fall 2009, program minus control.

context: Texas Summer Bridge randomized evaluation; implementation, enrollment and one-year academic outcomes remain distinct.
name: Texas Summer Bridge showed no statistically significant fall registration difference (+1.0 point; 77.4% versus 76.4%).
description: The fall-2009 enrollment result has p = .68 and standard error 2.4 percentage points. It is a null early registration finding, not proof of no later effect.

values.value: Percentage-point difference in registering for at least one fall-2009 course, program minus control.
